title: Pop Art: An Idea Becomes a Connected System

scenes.title: An idea becomes a connected system
scenes.purpose: A four-panel Pop Art comic page in which a single idea lights up, repeats, connects and becomes a system.
visuals: Stationary ink-navy page with two-tone diagonal stripes and a cobalt dot screen weighted to the corners (Canvas 2D)
Hero panel: yellow separation with a red luminance-based halftone screen that thins as the bulb's light grows (Canvas 2D)
Giant outlined lightbulb, cream starburst, and BING! lettering with a separate offset ink echo layer (SVG)
Right column of repeated panels: blue panel with a radiating bulb, red panel with two bulbs, a wire and ZAP!, and a yellow/blue-halftone panel with three wired bulbs
Heavy #171717 panel contours with cream keylines so they read on the dark page

beats.development: The caption box AN IDEA BECOMES... unrolls. The unlit cream bulb flashes to yellow with a scale punch, the red halftone thins into a lit halo around it, and the starburst bursts out behind it.
BING! slams in from 1.6x scale. Its black offset echo layer then separates down and right. The bulb in the blue panel pops in.
The blue panel's light rays draw on. Two bulbs slide toward each other inside the red panel, and the wire between them draws.
ZAP! pops in. The caption box A CONNECTED SYSTEM! unrolls, and three bulbs pop in one after another, each thinning the blue halftone around itself. The connecting wire draws, completing the system.
Reading hold on the fully settled four-panel page.

findings: Reveals follow reading order: hero panel, then the right column from top to bottom, with one sound-effect word per beat.
All motion settles by 2.65s, before the 2.7s target.
justifiedHolds: 2.65-3.0s final hold so all copy can be read on the complete page.

notes: Silent preview: no music, effects or voice. The beat cadence is a silent authored cue sequence (0.25 lamp flash, 0.85 BING!, 1.6 wire, 1.85 ZAP!, 1.95/2.07/2.19 system bulbs).
Background refresh: the scene-dependent ink-navy striped page replaces the previous cream page. Panel inks keep the style tokens #171717, #E8393E, #F1C932, #2671C6 and #FFF6D6.
Demonstrated technique: luminance-based halftone shading (no separate preview recipe was supplied). Dots sit on a fixed rotated grid, and only their radius follows a time-derived light field.
